newsitem.title: UK: Rentokil results boosted by BET acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Rentokil results boosted by BET acquisition.

text.p: Business services group Rentokil Initial Plc on Wednesday reported a 48 percent rise in pre-tax profit in its first full-year figures since the acquisition of rival BET.

With earnings per share up 20.5 percent at 17.13p from 14.22p a year before, the company -- whose activities range from pest control to security services -- met its long-standing self-imposed target to raise earnings by 20 percent each year.

However, Rentokil said the results had been affected by exceptional costs of 16.4 million stg related to the integration of former BET businesses, by management being diverted to integration tasks and by the strength of the pound.
The pre-tax figure would have been 3.2 million higher if average 1995 exchange rates had prevailed through 1996, Rentokil said.
Rentokil said the integration of the BET businesses had proceeded "rapidly and successfully in line with plans," adding that it expected "continued good growth" in 1997.
Pre-tax profit rose to 318 million stg from 214.5 a year before on turnover which rose to 2,340 million stg from 874.5 million. The dividend was raised 20.5 percent to 5.06p from 4.20.
Analysts had mostly expected pre-tax profits to be in a range between 317 million stg and 335 million stg. The dividend was expected at between 5.0p and 5.1p.

Net debt, which rose to 590 million stg following the BET acquisition, was reduced to 510 million stg by year end. Excluding the former BET businesses, turnover in Rentokil's old businesses rose 15 percent to 1.01 billion stg and profits rose nine percent to 233.4 million stg.
Rentokil said BET's operating margins were raised to 8.7 percent from 8.2 percent.
